caller_census.method: whole-.text scan for E8 calls, E9 tail jumps and RIP-relative LEA references landing on each target, validated by decoding forward from the enclosing FDE start with Capstone (census.py). A site counts only on a real instruction boundary with the expected mnemonic. A second raw scan without FDE validation agrees: the only hit in .text for any of the five scanned targets is the known Reset caller 0x61c1bdd -> 0x61c1a20.
notes: All four destructors have ZERO direct calls, tail jumps or LEA refs: they are vtable-only (slots 0/1 in each vtable). Destruction reaches them through a base-pointer delete, which dispatches through the vtable D0 slot.
D0 does NOT call D1: the D0 bodies inline the D1 steps (vptr store + engine free) and then tail-jump to sized operator delete. That is why D1 has no caller at all -- not even D0.
No LEA reference to any of the four functions exists in .text: the vtable slots are RELATIVE relocations, not LEA loads (see the two merged vtable packets).

cases.split: 600 compress-live + 600 uncompress-live (each 200 D1, 200 D0, 100 D1-then-D1 double-free, 100 D0-then-D1 use-after-free) + 600 null-ctx (150 per family per destructor) + 600 ordering/size (150 per family per destructor)
what_is_checked: d1: vptr stored first (0x64d7418 compress / 0x64d7448 uncompress), then the engine free on the ctx slot; the holder stays live and the ctx slot still holds the freed handle (the binary never nulls it)
d0: the same two events, then sized operator delete (0x70 / 0x38); the holder memory is freed and any later access raises
d0 does not call d1: a D0 trace has no d1 event (the steps are inlined); the vptr store still precedes the free
double destroy: D1-then-D1 double-frees the ctx (detected by the registry, never executed twice -- executing it would be UB in the test process); D0-then-D1 touches freed memory
null ctx: free(NULL) is a no-op in both engine frees, so a null-ctx destroy succeeds with a null-noop free event (the OOM path: createCCtx/createDCtx returning NULL)
ordering/size: vptr store is always event 0, the free is event 1, operator delete (D0 only) is last; delete sizes pin the holder sizes independently of the factory
the committed cases.tsv matches a fresh regeneration from the same seeded generator

observations: Both D1 bodies store the most-derived vtable address point BEFORE the engine free: a partially-destroyed object still dispatches virtually to its own class while its context is freed.

Both D0 bodies duplicate the D1 steps instead of calling D1 (45 B vs 36 B: the extra 9 B are push/pop rbx, the delete size immediate and the tail jump). The compiler inlined the complete-object destructor into the deleting destructor.

Neither destructor nulls the ctx slot after freeing it: a second D1 on the same holder would double-free the engine context. The model detects this via its registry and records it instead of executing the second real free.
The operator-delete sizes (0x70 / 0x38) independently confirm the holder sizes the factory packet established (0x70 compress, 0x38 uncompress) -- the sizes agree from two different functions.
The inBuffer (plain {src, size, pos} struct) needs no destruction: neither destructor touches +0x58..+0x70 / +0x20..+0x38.
